device.name: Antelope Discrete 4 Pro Synergy Core
device.notes: vid, pid and bcdDevice all read from the device's own Windows PnP instance id on a machine with the unit attached: USB\VID_23E5&PID_A2BF carries FriendlyName "Discrete 4 Pro Synergy Core", and HID\VID_23E5&PID_A2BF&REV_0203&MI_03 is the vendor-defined HID interface. The vid is no longer an assumption carried over from Orion Studio III. The per-unit serial is deliberately not recorded.

transport.notes: report_size is not assumed from Orion. The vendor format defines the 0x83 meter report as a 16-byte header plus afx_meters of ubyte * 304, which is exactly 320. Interface 3 is confirmed from the PnP instance id (MI_03), which names it a HID-compliant vendor-defined device. The endpoints are carried over from the family and are NOT separately confirmed on this unit. poll_interval_ms is left null on purpose: 29.5 reports/s was measured through Antelope's own TCP server, and that server decimates, so it is not the wire interval.
transport.evidence: Antelope's own machine-readable report format, shipped in plaintext beside the control panel at C:\Users\Public\.AntelopeAudio\discrete4_hybrid_tb3\panels\report_format_1.0.1 (macOS: /Users/Shared/...). It marks itself "authorative": true. Read 2026-08-31 from a machine with the unit attached.

command.notes: Every write in the vendor format carries header report_id 0x70 with ext2 and ext3 zero, and a field list whose first entry is the target id and whose second is the value: set_pre_gain is [id ubyte, gain byte] and set_pre_phantom is [id ubyte, phantom ubyte]. That gives the 16/17/18 shape directly. Byte 4 is a length, 16 + payload, not an opcode. WHAT IS NOT HERE: the selector byte itself. The format's payload_id is an index in Antelope's request table, a space running 0-41, and not the byte at offset 16 - captured command frames in this family carry 0x50, 0xa2, 0xd3 and 0xd4 there. Do not populate params[].id from payload_id. Naming: PROTOCOL.md §4a calls the two header words at @8 and @12 (category, index); Antelope's own format calls the same two fields ext2 and ext3. Same bytes, two vocabularies - this file uses PROTOCOL.md's.

state_report._comment: Offsets computed by bit-walking the vendor's declared 0x73 field list: 69 fields, 1824 bits, 228 bytes of payload, a 244-byte frame. Landing on a whole number of bytes is itself a check, and the Discrete 8 Pro's 66-field layout totals the same 1824.
state_report.notes: Three cross-checks before this was written down. (1) The field list was validated against live data: with the unit streaming through Antelope's own server, ten meter arrays came back at exactly the declared sizes - pm_line_out 6, pm_mixer_in 32, pm_adat_out 16, pm_HP1/3/4 two each - and pm_HP3 and pm_HP4 exist only on this model. (2) The status bit order matches what this repository already established by observation elsewhere: phantom mask 0x10 shift 4 and phase 0x40 shift 6 are identical. The format adds hpf at bit 5 and zero_cross at bit 7, which captures had not decoded. (3) bus_block_offset 28 is the value zen_go_sc.json already carries. STILL 'derived' AND NOT 'confirmed': no real 0x73 frame from this unit has been parsed with these offsets. The device does not emit one unprompted; it answers an init request. Promote on the first successful parse.
state_report.evidence: Antelope's own machine-readable report format, shipped in plaintext beside the control panel at C:\Users\Public\.AntelopeAudio\discrete4_hybrid_tb3\panels\report_format_1.0.1 (macOS: /Users/Shared/...). It marks itself "authorative": true. Read 2026-08-31 from a machine with the unit attached. Live field-size check via the vendor TCP server on port 2021.

provenance.method: vendor's own plaintext report format, read from the user's own disk
provenance.what_was_done: Opened a JSON file that Antelope's installer places on the machine of anyone who installs their software, at .AntelopeAudio/<slug>/panels/report_format_<version>. It is world-readable, not encrypted, not obfuscated, carries no licence header and no confidentiality marking, and needs no credentials. Reading it is what the vendor's own control panel does at startup.
what_was_NOT_done: No decompilation or disassembly of any Antelope binary.
No decryption, and no circumvention of any technical protection measure - there is none on this file.
No firmware modification, no firmware dump, no patching.
No credentials, no licence server, no account, nothing behind a login.
No redistribution of the vendor's file: only facts derived from it appear here.
No confidential or leaked material; nothing from an NDA or an internal source.
provenance.purpose: Interoperability: making hardware the owner has paid for controllable from their own operating system. Field offsets and parameter layouts are facts about an interface, not creative expression.
provenance.caveat: This records what was and was not done so the maintainer can judge it. It is not legal advice, and it is not a claim about any particular jurisdiction.

channels.notes: The vendor format's 0x73 preamps block is a struct of count 4, one status byte per preamp. Note that the preamp_gains array beside it is byte * 7, not 4. Recorded as read; the extra entries are not explained here and should not be rounded away.

buses.notes: The 0x73 volumes_and_mutes block is a struct of count 6, one byte each: volume in the low 7 bits, mute in the top bit. Names and ids for the six are not established here - only the shape and where it sits.

unresolved_state_offsets: The selector byte written at param_id_offset for each parameter. The vendor format gives field layouts but not that byte; it needs a capture or Antelope's own request table.
Which bus id maps to which physical output in the volumes_and_mutes block of 6.
Why preamp_gains is byte * 7 on a four-preamp device.
The wire interval of the 0x73 and 0x83 reports. 29.5/s was measured through the vendor's TCP server, which decimates.
